chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Gatemouth Moore served with a summons on stage at the Apollo
summary: Blues shouters Joe Turner and Wynonie Harris and preacher-singer Gatemouth Moore are praised. At the Apollo, Moore sang 'Mr. Landlord' as the lights went up, and a sheriff served him a nonsupport summons.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, Joe was doing a lot of those things we're talking about, you know? And, of course, Wynonie Harris. Man, those guys could sing (unintelligible) and they were rockin' and swingin' far more than what these guys are doing now. You know what I mean. They -- and they were doing it natural, you know. They had another singer called Reverend Gatemouth Moore. When I say Reverend, I mean he did eventually turn to preaching. But I remember when this particular Reverend Gatemouth Moore was singing these blues back in those days. He was booked into the Apollo Theater with Basie's band, man. And this thing about, 'Hey, Mr. Landlord, Turn up all the Lights, this house is going to get raided,' one of those things, tonight and one of those kind of things.
Funny thing happened. Now that reminded me of

something. He was at the Apollo Theater, and in those days -- I got to mention this and clarify it -- guys had to travel -- one nighters, you know, one of these things. So that made you neglect your family life quite a bit, as you and I well know. And you didn't get to see your family a lot. Well, anyway, Reverend Gatemouth Moore was one of those guys, and this is an incident that actually occurred.

I said He was This was Count Basie's band. We were there with Fletcher. And he was singing this particular thing we talked about, now, "Hey, Mr. Landlord, turn up all the lights or this house is gonna be raided and get rocked something, got to be ready, going to rock tonight," you know, and he had already told the electrician that operates the lights to do this when he said he'd tell them. So they turned up all the lights. And when they turned up all the lights, the sheriff was in the wings, and he had a summons from his wife for nonsupport. He hadn't seen her in months, and she found out that he was going to be in New York.

MR. HENDERSON: So when he finished breaking up the house and everything, he walked off the stage and got in the wings, and this guy said, "Hey, are you Gatemouth Moore? Yes, " He said, "Good, here's a summons for you." Yes, I'm Gatemouth, ~~(unintelligible)~~
And he was Fletcher's band man, and the guy -- so the next show he wasn't there, you know. He split. And when I say
split, you know what that means. He left.

So this was it. But getting back, man, he was a legend, though. That guy could sing. And he would come out on the stage in a derby, see. And he could actually preach, man. He could preach, this guy, all in rhythm, you know, blues and things like they don't do now. So this stuff about rock and roll didn't just start just recently.
